Labs are done in class, saved into your course GitHub repo, and submitted by posting your repo link on Courseworks. This page grows week by week.

## Week 1 (Sep 10)

- **[Lab 0a — Getting set up](lab0a.qmd)**: GitHub account, private course repo, LEAP hub · verification notebook: [verify_setup.ipynb](verify_setup.ipynb)
- **[Lab 0b — Python, just enough to start](lab0b_python_basics.ipynb)**: notebooks, numpy, matplotlib, a first look at pandas and xarray
- **[Lab 0c — The climate of NYC](lab0c_nyc_climate.ipynb)**: distributions, a hand-fit 3-parameter model, ERA5 vs CMIP6
- **[Lab 0d — A bucket](lab0d_bucket.ipynb)**: budgets, equilibrium, stepping forward in time

## Week 2 (Sep 17)

We covered the energy-balance models in lecture but did not reach the labs. Lab 1b moves to Week 3; Lab 1a is optional practice.

## Week 5 (Oct 8) {#week-5-oct-8}

We completed the Gregory lab and began discussing deep-ocean heat uptake and fast and slow climate responses.

- **Gregory plots from CMIP6:** diagnose radiative forcing and feedback from a climate-model experiment. <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/gregory_cmip6.ipynb" download>Download notebook</a>

**[Download the Gregory lab and supporting files](week05_labs.zip)** and unzip them before opening the notebook. The package includes saved CMIP6 annual means: set `USE_SAVED_MEANS = True` to use these instead of reading cloud data. Keep the `data` folder beside the notebook.

[Slides (PDF)](../slides/week05.pdf) · [Running instructions](week05_README.txt) · [Python packages](week05_requirements.txt)

## Week 6 (Oct 15) {#week-6-oct-15}

After discussing surface–deep-ocean heat uptake and two time scales, we will work with a one-dimensional energy balance model across latitude.

- **[Regional climate: a 1D energy balance model](latitude_ebm.ipynb)**: begin with an independent model at each latitude, compare with Earth's temperature and radiation patterns, then add horizontal heat transport. <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/latitude_ebm.ipynb" download>Download notebook</a>

All model code is supplied. Answer one short question after each section; Section 5 (diffusion alone) is optional.

**[Download the notebook and its data](week06_labs.zip)** and unzip them before opening the notebook. Keep the `data` folder beside it. The package includes the NCEP temperature file, so the lab can run offline; a missing file will be downloaded from NOAA when the notebook runs.

[Week 6 slides (PDF)](../slides/week06.pdf) · [Running instructions](week06_README.txt) · [Python packages](week06_requirements.txt)

## Week 8 (Oct 29) {#week-8-oct-29}

**Exploring the climate of CESM2:** inspect a CMIP6 simulation, compare monthly temperature with its climatology, calculate area-weighted averages, and examine the planetary energy budget.

- <a href="cesm2_exploration/exploring_cesm2.ipynb" download>Download the notebook</a>
- [Read the notebook with plots](cesm2_exploration/exploring_cesm2.html)

Open the notebook in the course Jupyter environment and run the cells in order. The data preparation code is included. The first run needs internet access and takes about one to two minutes to create the data file; later runs use the saved file. No separate data download is needed.

Pause at the **Guess before running** questions and complete the plotting exercise. [Python packages](cesm2_exploration/requirements.txt).
